topic: Token Usage Meters for Agent Cost Tracking

competitors.title: How to Measure AI Agent Token Usage (Tokenade)
key_points: Four distinct quantities must never be conflated: input tokens, output tokens, cached (cache-read) tokens, and dollar cost — they are priced very differently

Ground truth is the provider's `usage` object on every response (Anthropic: input_tokens, output_tokens, cache_creation_input_tokens, cache_read_input_tokens; OpenAI: prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, total_tokens) — never estimate with a character heuristic

Three places to read usage, increasing accuracy: vendor dashboard (daily aggregate, coarse), the agent's own counter (no attribution), and logging the per-call `usage` field with a label (the real meter)
Cost formula: cost = (input_tokens × input_price/MTok) + (cache_read_tokens × input_price × 0.10) + (output_tokens × output_price/MTok)
Cache-read tokens bill at ~10% of the input rate — two sessions with identical input volume can differ 9x in cost on cache-hit rate alone
Attribute usage to four cost drivers by labelling each call: file reads, tool output, the MCP manifest (a constant per-turn tax), and transcript replay
A worked example: 18 turns on Sonnet 5, 2.4M input tokens (1.6M cache reads) + 40K output = $2.32 for one task
Common mistakes: counting output and ignoring input, ignoring cache, estimating with the wrong tokenizer, measuring one call instead of the whole session

competitors.title: How to Track Token Cost Across LLM Workflows (Honeycomb)
key_points: Six-step process: capture usage from every model response → attach business metadata → compute cost at log time → store as request-level telemetry → build dashboards → alert on drift
Compute cost when the request is logged, not weeks later in a reporting job, because pricing tables, model names, cache rules, and tool charges change quickly
The OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions (`gen_ai.*`) are the vendor-neutral schema; do not build dashboards around each provider's raw field names

Reference event schema carries gen_ai.operation.name, gen_ai.request.model, gen_ai.response.model, gen_ai.usage.input_tokens, gen_ai.usage.cache_read_input_tokens, gen_ai.usage.output_tokens, gen_ai.response.finish_reasons, plus custom llm.request_cost_usd and llm.pricing_version
The spec deliberately does not define dollar cost — compute it yourself from token counts and a versioned price table kept next to the standard usage fields
Give every agent a unique `gen_ai.agent.name` (omit it and the span shows as Unknown); sub-agents get their own distinct names rather than inheriting the parent's
Let the caller emit the `invoke_agent` span, not the agent being called, so each agent's work and token spend stays separated

The most useful dashboard panel is often outlier requests — a single runaway request, huge context window, or retry loop distorts daily spend; alert on tokens per request, tokens per session, cost per feature, cost per workspace
Reconcile telemetry totals against provider invoices monthly

competitors.title: Usage — OpenAI Agents SDK
key_points: The Agents SDK automatically tracks token usage for every run; access via `result.context_wrapper.usage`

Tracked fields: requests, input_tokens, output_tokens, total_tokens, request_usage_entries (per-request breakdown), and details (input_tokens_details.cached_tokens, input_tokens_details.cache_write_tokens, output_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens)
Usage is aggregated across all model calls during the run, including model calls that produce tool calls or handoffs — the run is the natural metering boundary

`preserve_raw_usage` keeps the provider-specific usage payload (detached JSON snapshot) when an app must distinguish an omitted field from a provider-reported zero; the SDK does not aggregate raw_usage across the run
For streaming Chat Completions providers, an explicit usage request is needed: `ModelSettings(include_usage=True)`
With a Session, each `Runner.run(...)` returns usage for that specific run only, but prior messages are re-fed as input, so later turns carry larger input token counts

`RunResult.to_state()` snapshots usage accumulated so far; a resumed run starts from those totals — except nested `Agent.as_tool()` runs, whose post-resume usage deliberately rolls up into the outer run
RunHooks receive `context.usage`, so usage can be logged at lifecycle moments such as on_agent_end

competitors.title: Token & Cost Tracking — Langfuse
key_points: For every LLM generation Langfuse records two things, each broken down by usage type: usage details (units consumed per type) and cost details (USD per type)
Cost is either ingested from the LLM response or inferred: the model parameter is matched to a model definition holding a price per usage type, then multiplied by the observation's usage
Only generation and embedding observations carry usage/cost — other observation types do not
Usage keys must match exactly the keys in the model definition; custom model definitions are added in Project Settings > Models
Reasoning models require ingested usage — cost cannot be inferred for e.g. the OpenAI o1 family without token counts
Cost data feeds custom dashboards, threshold alerts, and the Metrics API for analytics, billing, and rate-limiting

competitors.title: Spend Tracking — LiteLLM Proxy
key_points: Automatic spend tracking for 100+ LLMs for keys, users, and teams, priced from a maintained model cost map
`max_budget` and `budget_duration` are set per key, user, or team, with `budget_reset_at` for the replenishment cycle — enforcement lives next to the meter, not in a separate reporting job
Provider-specific cost tracking is applied automatically when the response includes tier metadata (Vertex AI PayGo/priority pricing, Bedrock service tiers, Azure base model mapping)
`spend_logs_metadata` can be attached per key/team/request tag for attribution
Daily Spend Breakdown API (`/user/daily/activity?start_date=&end_date=`) returns granular usage by model, provider, and API key; `/global/spend/report` aggregates per-user spend
Model pricing data must be kept in sync from GitHub or reported costs diverge from the provider bill

stats.fact: OpenTelemetry's GenAI conventions moved out of the core semantic-conventions repository on 12 June 2026 (v1.42.0) into the dedicated open-telemetry/semantic-conventions-genai repository so the area could iterate faster than the core stability bar allows; as of October 2026 every gen_ai.* definition is still Development status (only inherited error.type, server.address, server.port are Stable), so attribute names can be renamed without a deprecation window

stats.fact: OTel splits token metering into two instrument families: usage counters (gen_ai.client.inference.usage.input_tokens / .output_tokens, plus cache_read, cache_write, reasoning subsets) for cumulative consumption and cost approximation, and per-operation histograms (gen_ai.client.inference.operation.input_tokens / .output_tokens) which must never be used for totals — a histogram with modality as a dimension returns p95 = 200 for 100 operations of 100 text + 200 image tokens whose true p95 is 300

OTel token counters carry a required gen_ai.token.modality attribute (text/image/audio/unknown), so summing across modality equals the total even for providers that report no breakdown; when a system reports both used and billable tokens, instrumentation MUST report billable tokens, and instrumentation that cannot obtain token counts efficiently MUST NOT report usage metrics

Recommended histogram boundaries are power-of-four: per-operation token histograms use [1, 4, 16, 64, 256, 1024, 4096, 16384, 65536, 262144, 1048576, 4194304, 16777216, 67108864]; gen_ai.invoke_agent.duration uses [0.1 … 409.6] seconds; gen_ai.client.operation.duration uses [0.01 … 81.92] seconds

Agent-level OTel instruments are gen_ai.invoke_agent.duration (Histogram, unit s), gen_ai.invoke_agent.inference_calls (Histogram, unit {inference_call}), gen_ai.invoke_agent.tool_calls (Histogram, unit {tool_call}, including failed calls), gen_ai.invoke_workflow.duration, and gen_ai.execute_tool.duration — distributions scoped to a single agent invocation

Cache-read tokens bill at roughly 10% of the normal input rate, so two sessions sending identical input volume can differ ~9x in cost on cache-hit rate alone; the worked example of 18 turns on Sonnet 5 with 2.4M input tokens (1.6M cache reads) + 40K output tokens costs $2.32

Anthropic's Usage & Cost Admin API reports usage with bucket_width=1d/1h/1m (default limits 7/24/60 buckets, maximum 31/168/1,440), groups by model, workspace_id, api_key_id, inference_geo, and speed (requires the fast-mode-2026-02-01 beta header), and exposes a separate /v1/organizations/cost_report endpoint in USD cents grouped by workspace_id or description (daily granularity only); data typically appears within 5 minutes with a recommended polling frequency of once per minute

The OpenAI Agents SDK meters per run: requests, input_tokens, output_tokens, total_tokens, per-request request_usage_entries, plus cached_tokens / cache_write_tokens / reasoning_tokens details; streaming Chat Completions providers need ModelSettings(include_usage=True) to return usage at all

In a sessioned agent (e.g. OpenAI Agents SDK with SQLiteSession) prior messages are re-fed as input on each run, so input token counts grow per turn even though each run's usage is reported independently — the per-call view hides the compounding that makes agent replay expensive

OpenMeter (Apache-2.0, YC W23, co-founded by ex-Stripe engineer Peter Marton, now Kong Konnect Metering & Billing) meters LLM tokens with a CloudEvents event (type prompt, data.tokens, subject=customer) aggregated SUM with groupBy provider/model/type, and self-hosting requires running PostgreSQL, ClickHouse, Kafka, and the API server as four separate components; named production users include Trigger.dev and Requestly

Langfuse cost tracking is infer-then-ingest: if the response carries cost it is used, otherwise the model name is matched to a price-per-usage-type model definition and multiplied by usage; reasoning models such as the OpenAI o1 family cannot have cost inferred and require ingested usage, and only generation/embedding observations carry usage or cost

Ecosystem adoption as of 2026-10-01 (GitHub): LiteLLM 59,970 stars (Apache/NOASSERTION, pushed 2026-10-01), Langfuse 35,256 (pushed 2026-10-01), MLflow 28,207 (Apache-2.0), OpenLLMetry/Traceloop 7,463 (Apache-2.0), Helicone 6,190 (Apache-2.0), OpenLIT 2,809 (Apache-2.0), OpenMeter 2,356 (Apache-2.0), OTel GenAI semconv repo 401 — i.e. the metering primitives are mature but the standard itself is still small and Development-status

angles: The missing-meter anti-pattern: teams optimize a number they have never actually looked at — you cannot cut what you do not measure, so step zero is producing real per-session numbers, not trimming context on a hunch

Four numbers, not one: input, output, cache-read, and dollars are priced so differently that a single 'tokens used' figure is actively misleading; a meter that does not break out cached input cannot tell you where the money went

Cost = tokens x price, and only the currency half is missing: token counts land automatically from the provider response, but no standard ships a dollar figure — you must own a versioned price table and compute cost at log time, because prices, model names, and cache rules change under you

The two-instrument rule (and the trap it prevents): counters for cumulative spend, histograms for per-operation outliers — putting a breakdown like modality on the histogram silently corrupts your p95 (200 instead of 300), which is exactly the kind of quiet wrongness a cost meter must not have

Metering boundary determines what you can bill: a meter per model call answers 'is this prompt expensive', a meter per run answers 'what did this task cost', and a meter per customer-subject answers 'what do I invoice' — pick the boundary before you pick the tool, because an agent run is not a request

Attribute the meter, don't just total it: tokens by category (file reads, unfiltered tool output, the always-present MCP manifest, transcript replay) turns an alarming total into a specific fix; the manifest in particular is a constant per-turn tax independent of the task

Cache-hit rate is the highest-leverage dial most teams never touch: a ~10% cache-read rate means the same input volume can cost 9x less, so prompt-cache hit rate belongs on the cost dashboard next to spend

Cost tracking without an enforcement edge is observability theatre: the same meter should feed a budget/reset cycle (max_budget + budget_duration, or an entitlements/credit balance) so a runaway loop trips a limit instead of an invoice

Two audiences, two schemas from one event: engineering needs request-level outliers and latency correlation, finance needs an immutable per-period aggregate that reconciles to the invoice — emit request-level telemetry once, and roll it up for both, instead of maintaining a monthly spreadsheet

The standard is young and the attribute names will move: gen_ai.* moved to its own repository in June 2026 and every GenAI attribute is still Development status, so pin the conventions version your dashboards assume and keep the price table versioned separately (llm.pricing_version) so a spec bump does not silently rewrite historical cost
